podcast.title: Origin and Early Invisibility (1994-1999)
podcast.body: Formed in Sydney, Australia, in 1994, The Vines remained almost completely invisible throughout the entire 1990s, with little public or industry interest. "They were born in Sydney, Australia in 1994. And for all of the 90s, they remained almost completely invisible."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Single Release and Hype (2001)
podcast.body: A single released in November 2001 generated incredible hype, marking a turning point in their career. "But then a single in November 2001. The hype was incredible."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Tonight Show" Rehearsal Trashing (December 2002)
podcast.body: In December 2002, The Vines secured a significant opportunity with a spot on "The Tonight Show with Jay Leno." However, during rehearsal, Craig Nicholls trashed the set, leading to the band being kicked off the show and losing one of their best chances to reach a new audience. "The Vines get a big break with the spot on the tonight show with Jay Leno. But during rehearsal, Craig trashed the set."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Brisbane Incident (September 2002)
podcast.body: In September 2002, an unexplained incident occurred in Brisbane, Australia, where Craig Nicholls reportedly bombarded passing cars with "big backs and flay o' fishes." "In September 2002, there was an unexplained incident in Brisbane, Australia where he bombarded passing cars with big backs and flay o' fishes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Incident with Record Label Executive (May 2002)
podcast.body: In May 2002, Craig Nicholls had a freak out on the band's bus when an executive from The Vines' record label brought several people to meet him. "There was that incident in May of 2002 when he freaked out at an executive from the Vines record label who brought some people to meet Craig on the bus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rolling Stone Cover (2002)
podcast.body: In October 2002, the band was featured on the cover of Rolling Stone magazine, under the headline "Rock is back. Meet the Vines," symbolizing the perceived return of rock music. "In October 2002, they appeared on the cover of Rolling Stone. The headline was, Rock is back. Meet the Vines."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Coca-Cola Paranoia (April 2003)
podcast.body: In April 2003, Craig Nicholls refused to drink any Coca-Cola. He claimed that his image had mysteriously manifested itself on a Coke can while on the tour bus. "April 2003, Craig refuses to drink any Coca-Cola after he says his image mysteriously manifested itself on a Coke can on the tour bus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: On-Stage Brawl in Boston (January 2003)
podcast.body: In January 2003, during a gig in Boston, Craig Nicholls and bass player Patrick Matthews engaged in a brawl on stage. "January 2003, Craig and bass player Patrick Matthews get into a brawl on stage during a gig in Boston."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Australian Origins and McDonald's Meeting
podcast.body: The Vines were formed in Sydney, Australia, in 1994. Singer and guitarist Craig Nichols and bass player Patrick Matthews met while working together at their local McDonald's. "They were formed in Sydney, Australia in 1994, when singer and guitarist Craig Nichols and bass player Patrick Matthews met while working at their local McDonald's."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

podcast.title: Comparisons to Nirvana
podcast.body: The Vines and their lead singer, Craig Nicholls, were frequently compared to Nirvana and Kurt Cobain. One English newspaper even featured them on its cover with the caption, "The Screwed Up Story of the Best Band Since Nirvana." "you'll find a lot of comparisons between the Vines and Nirvana and Craig and Kurt."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Craig Nicholls' Dislike of Live Performance
podcast.body: Craig Nicholls reportedly "hates to play live" and prefers to work in the studio. His aversion to live performances often manifests in destructive behavior during Vines gigs, with him leading the smashing of equipment. "Craig hates to play live. He'd rather just mess around in the studio if that's okay with everyone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Craig Nicholls' Drug and Alcohol Use
podcast.body: Lead singer Craig Nicholls reportedly consumes a lot of drugs and appears to be drunk almost all the time. There is also a rumor that he eats at McDonald's at least once a day. "He apparently takes lots of drugs. He seems to be drunk almost all the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Debut Recording in Los Angeles
podcast.body: The significant hype from their 2001 single led to an offer for the band to fly to Los Angeles to record their debut record. "That was enough for The Vines to get an offer to fly to Los Angeles to record a debut record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Eccentric Frontman Craig Nichols
podcast.body: Lead singer Craig Nichols was described as an eccentric frontman whose erratic behavior became part of the band's story. He reportedly smoked a lot of dope, insisted on eating at McDonald's at least once a day, and was volatile both in interviews and on stage. His behavior was later explained by a diagnosis of Asperger syndrome, a form of autism. "Their story was the help of the fact that they had an eccentric frontman in the form of Craig Nichols."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Meeting Revival Criteria
podcast.body: The Vines met the emerging criteria for indie rock bands at the time, possessing a name that began with "The," playing "shouty, riffy, punky songs," and having an appealing look and attitude that music journalists were eager to promote to resurrect rock. "They met the criteria. They had a name that began with The, which was the thing at the time. They played shouty, riffy, punky songs. And they had a look at attitude that music journalists, desperate to resurrect Rock, could get behind."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nirvana Influence
podcast.body: Both Craig Nichols and Patrick Matthews were huge fans of Nirvana, specifically drawing inspiration from the parts of Nirvana's catalog where Kurt Cobain stripped everything down to the basics. This foundational influence shaped The Vines' own musical approach. "Both were huge fans of Nirvana and wanted to do something like that. Specifically, the parts of the Nirvana canon were Kurt stripped everything down to the basics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

podcast.title: Part of Indy Rock Revival
podcast.body: The Vines were explicitly named as a band that, alongside The Strokes, The White Stripes, the Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Interpol, The Hives, and Arcade Fire, was a firm part of the Indy Rock Revival in the late 2003/early 2004 period. "The strokes were firmly part of the Indy Rock Revival that also included the white stripes, the yay-yayas, interpole, the vines, the hives, and this new band called Arcade Fire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pre-Show Bathroom Ritual
podcast.body: Craig Nicholls has a reputation for locking himself in the bathroom for up to three hours before a show. "then there's his reputation of locking himself in the bathroom for up to three hours before a show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Quality of Music
podcast.body: Despite their frontman's erratic nature, the band's music was consistently described as good. "In the meantime though, the music was good. It was good."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sydney, Australia Origin
podcast.body: The Vines are described as a "much hyped band from Sydney, Australia," known for producing "pretty solid music." "The Vines are this much hype band from Sydney, Australia who put out some pretty solid music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Erratic Behavior and Asperger Syndrome (2001-2005)
xref.body: Around 2001-2002, as The Vines gained traction in North America, Craig Nichols began exhibiting serious erratic behavior, including unusual habits like insisting on eating at McDonald's daily, and violent outbursts against journalists, audiences, and bandmates, which led to legal issues. He was officially diagnosed with Asperger's in 2005 and agreed to therapy. "We started hearing about some serious erratic behavior... In 2005, he was officially diagnosed in agreed to therapy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bizarre Habits and Early Career Issues
xref.body: When The Vines emerged in 2001, singer Craig Nicholls was noted for unusual behaviors, such as an insistence on eating at McDonald's at least once daily, a habit he maintains today, along with KFC. More significantly, he displayed severe temper issues directed at bandmates, journalists, photographers, fans, and strangers. "When the Vine's first appeared in 2001, we started hearing about Craig's bizarre habits, like insisting that he had to eat at McDonald's at least once a day."
